o.norm: gg is not combo, but 8811 could conflict with NestedGreaterGreater or others

i.norm: Tests that HTML entities resolving to multi-codepoint sequences (e.g. ⋙̸ → ⋙ + combining stroke) are correctly unescaped and that re-escaping produces the canonical entity names.

Several "greater-than" related named entities can map to the same base character (U+226B ≫), while others like ⋙̸ and ≫⃒ expand to two codepoints (base char + combining overlay). After unescaping these entities and then re-escaping back to ASCII using the extended escape mode, the output should use the canonical entity name (≫ for U+226B) plus numeric references for any combining characters that have no standalone named entity. A final unescape of the re-escaped string must reproduce the original unescaped Unicode text, confirming a lossless round-trip through escape → unescape.

Input: six named entities that all involve U+226B (MUCH GREATER-THAN, ≫). ⋙̸ and ≫̸ are "negated" forms that add a combining stroke (U+0338 ̸) after ≫. ≫⃒ adds a different combining overlay (U+20D2 ⃒) after ≫. ≫, ≫, and ≫ are three different names for the plain ≫ character.

Expected Unicode string after unescaping all six entities. ≫ (U+226B) — from ≫ ⋙̸ (U+22D9 + U+0338) — from ⋙̸ (triple-greater + combining long solidus) ≫⃒ (U+226B + U+20D2) — from ≫⃒ (much-greater + combining long vertical line) ≫̸ (U+226B + U+0338) — from ≫̸ (much-greater + combining long solidus) ≫ (U+226B) — from ≫ ≫ (U+226B) — from ≫

Re-escape the Unicode string to ASCII using the extended entity set. The encoder uses canonical names: ≫ for U+226B and ⋙ for U+22D9. Combining characters (U+0338, U+20D2) have no named entity, so they become numeric hex refs.
Verify round-trip: unescaping the re-escaped form reproduces the original Unicode text.
